main: ruleset: pull request required, status check er-check required, no bypass actors. It was disabled once, for the merge that put a stale docs/er.md on main (the setup for the push and open-PR runs), then enabled again.

observations.claim: A pull request that changes schema/schema.sql without regenerating docs/er.md fails the er-check job at 'git diff --exit-code'; mergeStateStatus is BLOCKED and a merge is refused ('the base branch policy prohibits the merge')
A pull request head whose docs/er.md was regenerated passes er-check (this run came before the stale commit that made it red)
The first red run was an unresolvable action name (k1LoW/install-tbls-action), not staleness; the correct action is k1LoW/setup-tbls
A workflow with contents: write pushing the regenerated file to main is rejected: GH013 'Changes must be made through a pull request' and 'Required status check er-check is expected'
Opening a pull request with the built-in token fails by default: 'GitHub Actions is not permitted to create or approve pull requests'; the setting can_approve_pull_request_reviews was false

After enabling that setting the pull request opens; the er-check run for it is created with conclusion action_required and 0 jobs, so the PR has no check and stays BLOCKED until a person approves the run (POST /actions/runs/{id}/approve); after approval er-check ran and passed, and the PR merged
With has_wiki true, git ls-remote on <repo>.wiki.git answers 'Repository not found' until the first page is created in the web UI; afterwards it answers

A workflow with contents: write clones the wiki with the built-in token and pushes a page; no pull request, no ruleset change; the page renders the Mermaid block; no pull request check covers the page; the workflow was started by workflow_dispatch and copies the committed docs/er.md without regenerating it
upload-artifact stores docs/er.md and the SVG: 5935 bytes zipped, expires 90 days after the run, download URL answers 401 without credentials; started by workflow_dispatch

POST /pages with build_type workflow enables Pages; a workflow with pages: write and id-token: write deployed an SVG; the URL answers 200 without credentials (the repository is public); started by workflow_dispatch
github.com renders the Mermaid block of docs/er.md as a diagram (images/er-diagram-from-schema-file/github-rendered.png)
The pull request with the stale diagram was merged while the ruleset was disabled (merge at 06:28:11Z, ruleset updated 06:28:13Z), so that main held a stale docs/er.md for the push and open-PR runs

note: experimentCommit is the sandbox main when the wiki, Pages and artifact runs were made; the benchmark/ folder was added to the sandbox afterwards (the article links that later commit).

privateRepo.note: A private twin of the sandbox (same files as public main faa235a). The account's plan is not exposed by the API; rulesets, Pages and wikis worked on a private repository, so it is not GitHub Free (docs: those are paid-plan features in private repositories).

observations.claim: The same ruleset (pull request and er-check required) can be created on the private repository and is enforced: a direct push to main is rejected with GH013 'Changes must be made through a pull request'
er-check runs on a pull request in the private repository and passes; mergeStateStatus CLEAN
upload-artifact works; the download URL answers 401 without credentials; run duration 33 s

POST /pages with build_type workflow succeeds on the private repository and reports public: true; the deployed SVG answers 200 without credentials while the repository page and raw.githubusercontent.com file answer 404; run duration 44 s
The wiki is available; the first page is created in the web UI as in the public repository; the workflow then pushes docs/er.md with the built-in token; the wiki page answers 404 without credentials
github.com draws the Mermaid block of docs/er.md for a signed-in user with access
